children: Consumer confidence data in Poland sent mixed signals in September, as consumers rated their current situation more favourably while forecasts regarding the future deteriorated, figures published by the statistics office showed on Thursday.
The current consumer confidence indicator (BWUK) rose by 0.5 points from August to -10.8, suggesting a slight improvement in households' assessment of current conditions.

The increase was driven mainly by a stronger assessment of the ability to make major purchases. Consumers also viewed the current economic situation of the country somewhat more positively than a month earlier.
However, households became more pessimistic about their own financial situation. Assessments of both current and future household finances deteriorated compared with August.
Meanwhile, the leading consumer confidence indicator (WWUK), which measures expectations for the coming months, fell by 0.3 points to -7.9. This points to greater caution about the economic outlook.
The decline was mainly due to weaker expectations regarding household finances and unemployment. Consumers expect the labour market to worsen slightly over the next 12 months.
Compared with September 2025, both confidence indicators were weaker, indicating that consumer sentiment remains below last year's levels despite recent improvements.
Both consumer confidence indexes can range from minus 100 to plus 100.
Inflation expectations rose in September, the statistical office also reported. The proportion of consumers expecting price increases over the next 12 months rose to 27.2, up from 22.9 in August.
